removed: Having a baby is exciting, but it can also be exhausting, especially if it’s your first child. No matter how much experience you have with babies, you may be unsure of how to best care for one. But by keeping your newborn fed, clean, cozy, and well-rested, you can care for and have a happy baby!
[[Category:Baby Health]]
== Steps ==
===Meeting Baby’s Basic Needs===

#Feed your little one. Nutrition is one of the key parts of having a happy and thriving baby. Feed your little one according to a set schedule and their age, which can help them grow and keep them active and happy.[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Choose to [[Breastfeed|breast]] or [[Bottle Feed Babies|bottle feed]] newborns and infants.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20047741</ref> Breastfeeding is recommended because it offers the most benefits for your baby.<ref>http://americanpregnancy.org/breastfeeding/breastfeeding-and-bottle-feeding/</ref> Most newborns need eight to 12 feedings per day.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20047741</ref> After five to six months, most babies can have breast milk or formula and begin to eat cereal or mashed foods, which are sometimes called semi-solid foods.
#*Burp your baby after feeding for a few minutes to help dissipate gas in their system.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#*Figure out if your baby is getting enough to eat by making sure they produce at least six wet diapers and several bowel movements daily.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref> Your baby should also be gaining about five to seven ounces every week for the first six months of life. Between six to 12 months, your baby should gain about three to five ounces per week.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/expert-answers/infant-growth/faq-20058037</ref>
#*Ask your pediatrician questions about when it is best to begin semi-solids and solids, as well as drinking water.

#Change your baby’s diapers as necessary. It’s important to make sure that your baby has clean diapers, which promotes their health, can keep them happy, and help you when it comes time to potty train them. Whether you are using cloth or disposable diapers, change your baby’s diaper as soon as you realize it is soiled.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Lay your baby flat on their back to change the diaper. Keep a close eye on them at all times and never leave them alone on the changing table.
#*Remove the soiled diaper and gently wipe your baby’s genital area clean with wipes or a pre-moistened washcloth. Wipe baby girls from front to back to minimize the risk of urinary tract infections.
#*Be aware that removing a diaper too quickly from a baby boy may cause him to urinate.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#*Place a new diaper under your baby and apply an ointment made for the diaper area before fastening up the diaper. Your doctor can give you suggestions about ointments to use. These ointments often feature zinc oxide as the main ingredient. Applying an ointment can help to prevent diaper rash.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Wash your hands after changing the diaper.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#Bathe your baby regularly. Give your baby a bath a couple of times a week or if they have a diaper blowout that wipes cannot clean.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref> This can ensure that their skin stays clean without drying out.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Allow your baby’s stomach to calm for a bit if you want to bathe them after a feeding.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>

#*Have a washcloth, towel with a hood, mild, unscented baby shampoo and soap, baby wipes, a clean diaper, and clean clothes ready before their bath.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref> This can help you focus solely on the baby and not gathering items once you’ve started.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>
#*Consider a sponge bath if you don’t want to use a tub every time.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>

#*Fill the tub with 2-3 inches (5-8 centimeters) of warm water. Pour the warm water on your baby throughout the bath to keep them warm.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref> The water should be around 100F (38 degrees Celsius) and lower than 120F (49C) to prevent scalding.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438?pg=2</ref>

#*Support your baby, including the head, throughout the bath so that they doesn’t slip and hurt themself.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438?pg=2</ref>
#*Focus on washing inside skin folds, especially on the face, neck, and diaper area.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>

#*Wrap your baby in a towel with a hood when you’re finished to keep them warm and cozy.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438?pg=2</ref>

#*Massage baby with hypoallergenic lotion if you like.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438?pg=2</ref> This can calm them and give you a nice bonding experience.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#Clip your baby’s nails. Babies need short nails to minimize the risk of scratching or cutting their delicate skin.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/trimming-nails.html</ref> Because babies’ nails grow quickly, trim or file your baby’s nails once or twice a week, or more often if necessary.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/trimming-nails.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Use baby nail scissors or a small emery board. These are gentler and safer to use on a fidgety or squirming baby.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/trimming-nails.html</ref>

#*Consider asking your partner, a friend, or a family member to help you trim your baby’s nails. This may minimize the risk of cutting them.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/trimming-nails.html</ref>

#*Apply pressure to your baby’s finger if you accidentally cut it and draw blood. This is normal and you shouldn’t worry. Don’t use a bandage, which a baby may choke on if it gets into their mouth.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/trimming-nails.html</ref>

#Monitor your baby's umbilical cord stump. The umbilical cord is essential while your baby is in the womb, but after birth it is not necessary. Your baby's doctor will clamp what is left of the cord and it will fall off on its own in about two weeks.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/umbilical-cord/art-20048250</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*You should keep the umbilical cord area clean and dry until it falls off, but you do not need to clean it unless it looks crusty or sticky. If you notice a crusty or sticky discharge around the umbilical cord stump, then clean it with a bit of warm water and pat dry with a clean, dry towel.
#*Do not try to pull off the stump! Allow it to fall off on its own.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/umbilical-cord/art-20048250?pg=2</ref>

#Care for your baby boy's circumcision site. If you have a newborn son and you decide to have him circumcised, then you will need to monitor and clean the circumcision site while it heals. It takes about seven to 10 days for a circumcision wound to heal and during this time the wound is susceptible to infection.[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Check the area each time you change your baby's diaper. Clean off any stool or urine that gets on your baby's penis with some mild, unscented soap and warm water.
#*If you notice swelling, redness, or a cloudy, crusty fluid, then call your doctor. Your baby's circumcision wound may be infected.
===Helping a Baby Sleep===

#Learn your baby’s sleep requirements. Sleep is integral to a baby’s health and well-being. Learning how much they need can keep them happy and healthy.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref> The recommended daily sleep needs for babies are:[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Infants 0-2 months need 10.5-18 hours every day.
#*Babies 2-12 months need 14-15 hours every day.

#Follow a regular bedtime. Fix a regular bedtime for your baby that includes a routine. This can promote and regulate sleep and help relax it.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Keep in mind that most babies don't have a specific bedtime in the first two to three months of life because they are still feeding every few hours.
#*Take naps, feedings, baths, and your baby’s age when figuring out their bedtime.
#*Adjust your schedule for activities or other factors like illness.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>

#Get your baby to relax before bed. Babies usually need time to switch into bedtime mode. Help your little one relax with a bedtime routine and cozy environment.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Start switching into bedtime mode at least two hours before bedtime.
#*Dampen any noise.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>
#*Dim the lights in any spaces your baby might be. This signals them that it’s time to sleep.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>

#*Gently talk to your baby and rub their back to relax. This can also help soothe them if they are fussy.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>

#Establish a bedtime routine. Set up a nightly ritual at bedtime.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref> Taking a bath, nursing or feeding, reading a story, singing, or listening to soothing music can signal your baby that it’s time to sleep.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 10 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Reading or singing can help calm your baby.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>
#*Give them a warm bath to stimulate sleepiness. A gentle massage may encourage somnolence and prepare them for sleep.

#Create a cozy sleeping environment. Create a room for your baby that helps them to sleep. Factors such as temperature, white noise, and shutting out light can put them on the road to a full night’s rest.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 11 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*A room temperature between 60 and 75 degrees is optimal for promoting sleep.
#*Remove electronics or anything else that might stimulate your baby.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>
#*Use soft bulbs and curtains or blinds to control light. A night light in a non-stimulating color like red can reassure a baby.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>
#*White noise machine can dampen noises and help them sleep.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref>

#*Remove blankets and soft items from the crib or bassinet to minimize the risk of suffocation.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>

#Put your baby down while awake. Put your baby in their bed when they are drowsy but still awake. This helps them associate the crib or bassinet with sleep.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref> In addition, it may also reduce the amount of nighttime care you provide.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 12 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Lay your baby on their back in their bed.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>
#*Let your baby to adjust and see if they fall back asleep if they rouse when you put them in the bed. If they don't, hold them until they become drowsy.
===Keeping Baby Safe, Happy, and Stimulated===

#Promote bonding with your baby. Establishing a bond with your baby as a newborn and throughout infancy is an important part of promoting their health and development. From soothing, cradling, and eventually playing with your baby, do activities that promote a bond between you and your child.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref> You can bond with and stimulate your baby through a variety of activities including:[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 13 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Massage or gentle stroking
#*Vocal stimulation such as talking, singing, reading, or cooing.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Maintaining eye to eye contact at close range.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Playing with age-appropriate toys.

#Soothe a cranky baby. Most babies will invariably get cranky at times. Soothing them as they cry can help them to calm down and promote your bonding.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 14 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid sudden movements, bright lights, and loud noises so that you don’t startle your baby.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Pick your baby up if they cannot calm down from crying.
#*Stroke their skin and speak to them in a soft voice to help them calm down.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Swaddling newborns and babies under two months can help soothe them.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#Secure your baby in carriers. No matter if you are using a carrier, car seat, or stroller, make sure that your baby is securely fastened into the unit. This can prevent injuries or even death.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 15 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Learn how to properly secure your baby in carriers, strollers, and car seats. Most hospital will not allow you to leave without an appropriate car seat that you can properly use.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*Ask questions about using carriers, strollers, and car seats as you need. You can also read packaging instructions.
#*Limit activities that are too rough or bouncy, which can be dangerous for a baby.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#Ask for help. Many people feel overwhelmed when caring for a baby. Ask your partner, friends, or family members to help you care for your baby on occasion or when you need it. You may want to consider hiring a reputable babysitter you trust to give you some me time, too.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 16 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*Know that it’s okay to ask for help and that many people are willing to help out with babies.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>
#*If you don’t have any close friends or family to help you, your doctor or local hospital may help you find someone to help you.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/guide-parents.html</ref>

#Visit your pediatrician. Schedule regular doctor’s visits for your baby. In addition, if you have any questions or concerns, contact the pediatrician’s office. It’s better to be safe and ask questions than have something turn into a problem. Talk to your doctor right away if you think your baby has a fever or seems ill or is injured in any way.[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 17 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*Schedule regular doctor’s visits for your baby. Your pediatrician will check that they are thriving and developing according to schedule. In addition, the doctor will make sure your child is vaccinated against diseases.

#*Your baby should see their pediatrician at regular intervals including: at birth, three to five days old, two to four weeks, two months, four months, six months, nine months, one year, 15 months, and 18 months.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/checkups.html</ref>

#*Note what each visit will entail so that nothing comes as a surprise. For example, at three to five days your doctor will check your baby’s weight, length and head circumference and ask questions about feedings, sleeping habits, and defecation.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/checkup-2weeks.html</ref> At two months, your baby will receive his first round of vaccines. At nine months, your doctor will check your baby’s size and developmental issues such as speaking, standing, and playing peek-a-boo.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/checkup-9mos.html</ref>

added: #Feed your little one. Nutrition is one of the key parts of having a happy and thriving baby. Feed your little one according to a set schedule and their age, which can help them grow and keep them active and happy.[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Change your baby’s diapers as necessary. It’s important to make sure that your baby has clean diapers, which promotes her health, can keep her happy, and help you when it comes time to potty-train her. Whether you are using cloth or disposable diapers, change your baby’s diaper as soon as you realize it is soiled.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/guide_parents.html#</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 2.jpg|center]]

#Bathe your baby regularly. Give your baby a bath a couple of times a week or if she has a diaper blowout that wipes cannot clean.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref> This can ensure that her skin stays clean without drying out.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 3.jpg|center]]

#Clip your baby’s nails. Babies need short nails to minimize the risk of scratching or cutting their delicate skin.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/trimming_nails.html</ref> Because babies’ nails grow quickly, trim or file your baby’s nails once or twice a week, or more often if necessary.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/trimming_nails.html</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 4.jpg|center]]

#Learn your baby’s sleep requirements. Sleep is integral to a baby’s health and well-being. Learning how much she needs can keep her happy and healthy.<ref>http://www.sleepforkids.org/html/sheet.html</ref> The recommended daily sleep needs for babies are:[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Follow a regular bedtime. Fix a regular bedtime for your baby that includes a routine. This can promote and regulate sleep and help her relax her.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Get your baby to relax before bed. Babies usually need time to switch into bedtime mode. Help your little one relax with a bedtime routine and cozy environment.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Establish a bedtime routine. Set up a nightly ritual at bedtime.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref> Taking a bath, nursing or feeding, reading a story, singing, or listening to soothing music can signal your baby that it’s time to sleep.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Create a cozy sleeping environment. Create a room for your baby that helps her to sleep. Factors such as temperature, white noise, and shutting out light can put her on the road to a full night’s rest.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 9.jpg|center]]

#Put your baby down while awake. Put your baby in her bed when she is drowsy but still awake. This helps her associate the crib or bassinette with sleep.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref> In addition, it may also reduce the amount of nighttime care you provide.<ref>http://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/baby-sleep/art-20045014?pg=2</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 10.jpg|center]]

#Promote bonding with your baby. Establishing a bond with your baby as a newborn and throughout infancy is an important part of promoting her health and development. From soothing, cradling, and eventually playing with your baby, do activities that promote a bond between you and your child.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/guide_parents.html#</ref> You can bond with and stimulate your baby through a variety of activities including:[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Soothe a cranky baby. Most babies will invariably get cranky at times. Soothing her as she cries can help her to calm down and promote your bonding.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/guide_parents.html#</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 12.jpg|center]]

#Secure your baby in carriers. No matter if you are using a carrier, car seat, or stroller, make sure that your baby is securely fastened into the unit. This can prevent injuries or even death.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/guide_parents.html#</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 13.jpg|center]]

#Ask for help. Many people feel overwhelmed when caring for a baby. Ask your partner, friends, or family members to help you care for your baby on occasion or when you need it. You may want to consider hiring a reputable babysitter you trust to give you some me time, too.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/pregnancy_center/newborn_care/guide_parents.html#</ref>[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Visit your pediatrician. Schedule regular doctor’s visits for your baby. In addition, if you have any questions or concerns, contact the pediatrician’s office. It’s generally better to be safe and ask questions than have something turn into a problem.[[Image:Care for a Baby Step 15.jpg|center]]

added: Having a baby is exciting, but it can also be exhausting, especially if it’s your first child. No matter how much experience you have with babies, you may be unsure of how to best care for one. But by keeping your newborn fed, clean, cozy, and well-rested you can care for and have a happy baby!

#*Your baby should see her doctor at regular intervals including: at birth, 3-5 days old, 1 month, 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 9 months, 1 year, 15 months, and 18 months.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/growth/medical/checkups.html</ref>

#*Note what each visit will entail so that nothing comes as a surprise. For example, at 3-5 days your doctor will check your baby’s weight, length and head circumference and ask questions about feedings, sleeping habits, and defecation.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/system/Checkupsubcat/checkup_2weeks.html</ref> At 9 months, you doctor will check your baby’s size and developmental issues such as speaking, standing, and playing peek-a-boo.<ref>http://kidshealth.org/parent/system/Checkupsubcat/checkup_9mos.html</ref>

added: #  Buy everything you need for the baby. You need to have enough money in order to take care of the baby. Buy a highchair, playpen, a few toys, milk bottles, baby food, some clothes, maybe a pacifier, Oct, nappies or diapers, and many other things. Your baby will become a child after a few years so make sure that you have a reliable source of financial support for at least 16 years.

#  Feed the baby. Make sure your baby likes the food that you buy for him or her. If you do not have enough money to buy more baby food, you should have a baby food maker in handy. Milk is a great food for babies. You can [[Breastfeed|breast]] or [[Bottle Feed Babies|bottle feed.]] Ensure you follow the instructions on the packaging when making up infant formula. Bottles, tests etc should be sterilized.

#  Set the baby to sleep. Put him or her in a playpen or crib and lay a sheet and a blanket on the baby. Put a stuffed animal if needed. Don't forget the pillow. If the baby can't sleep, sing a lullaby. Your baby should be asleep in two to five minutes. Do not use a pillow if you are concerned about SIDS, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome, there is anecdotal evidence suggesting a link. Babies should be set to sleep so there's nothing in the cot or crib which could be a suffocation risk.

#  Change his or her diapers. If your baby goes to the bathroom in his or her diaper, set him or her on a cot or changing board. Take off the Velcro of the diaper and slide off the diaper from his or her bottom. Take a pair of fresh diapers out of a bag and put it under the baby's bottom. Attach the Velcro on. Use cloth diapers if you prefer. Remember there are different types of diapers for male and female babies which you may like to use. Clean all faecal matter from your baby's skin before you put on the clean diaper.

#  Get the baby to play. Put the baby in a playpen, crib or bedroom. Get a toy and give it to the baby. If the baby likes it, let her or him play with it. If the baby does not like it, put it away and repeat until the baby likes the toy. Remember, new born babies don't play. Your baby may be several months old before it displays an interest in toys.
#  Pay attention to your baby's needs and requirements. Child neglect and cruelty are criminal offences.[[Image:We have a baby...for awhile at least.jpg|center]]

added: == Tips ==
*When a baby won't stop crying, try these coping mechanisms:
*Does the baby need a 'check-in?' (e.g., eye contact, a smile, to be picked up and cuddled briefly)
*Does the baby need a position change?
*Does the baby need a diaper change?
*Is the baby hungry?
*Is the baby cold/too warm?
*Does the baby need to burp?
*Are the baby's clothes uncomfortable - Too tight?  Wadded up?  Rubbing?
*If none of these is the cause, undress the baby completely and check its entire body, including feet, toes.
*In other words - What are the baby's needs?  It may be any one or a combination of things.
